forces.title: High financing costs subdue EU construction sector momentum
forces.description: Higher interest rates and increased financing costs are making households and businesses more cautious about investing in new property. This is a significant factor capping growth momentum in Europe's construction sector, particularly affecting the building sector which remains a weak spot. It also makes it harder for governments and private investors to absorb further cost increases from contractors.
forces.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

forces.title: Infrastructure investment drives growth in European construction sector
forces.description: Infrastructure investment, strongly supported by EU funds and spending on energy and digital networks, is providing a crucial offset to the weak building sector across Europe. This includes specialized construction benefiting from renovation and sustainability projects, as well as broader infrastructure developments. Increased government spending on infrastructure is a key driver for stability and modest growth in the overall construction output.
forces.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

forces.title: Rising energy-intensive material prices pressure construction margins
forces.description: Higher energy prices are pushing up production costs for energy-intensive materials such as concrete, cement, and bricks, although the overall rise in material prices is gradual. This creates a significant challenge for contractors, as passing these higher input costs through the value chain is becoming increasingly difficult. Customers, facing higher interest rates, are less able to absorb further cost increases, leading to potential project profitability issues.
forces.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

forces.title: Stagnating residential building permits signal delayed housing recovery
forces.description: After a period of increase, the issuance of building permits for new dwellings in the EU has broadly stabilised, suggesting a fading momentum in the residential sector. This indicates that a stronger residential recovery will be delayed, as permits typically precede home completions by one to two years. Factors like higher interest rates, geopolitical uncertainty, and increased energy-intensive material costs are contributing to this slowdown.
forces.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

forces.title: Stricter renovation standards boost demand for energy-efficient construction
forces.description: Increasingly stringent renovation requirements for properties are encouraging buyers to pay closer attention to future renovation costs and energy performance. This trend, reinforced by higher energy costs, improves the economics of investments in insulation, high-performance glazing, and efficient heating systems. As a result, energy efficiency is becoming a critical determinant of property value and marketability, driving demand for related building products and construction services.
forces.source_title: Second-quarter resilience masks a more challenging outlook for Belgian housing

forces.title: Rising operating costs pressure Dutch road transport profitability
forces.description: Dutch road freight operators face mounting cost pressure from higher wages, a 30% diesel price surge, and the new truck charging scheme introduced in July 2026, which adds 7-8% to total transport costs. While rate increases help offset some costs, a temporary lag in contractually passing on fuel surcharges affects profitability. These cumulative impacts necessitate tight margin management and rapid pricing adjustments to avoid liquidity pressures.
forces.source_title: Dutch road transport gains momentum despite truck charge

forces.title: Global trade disruptions maintain longer, costlier shipping routes
forces.description: Disruptions in critical maritime passages like the Red Sea, Black Sea, Strait of Hormuz, and Panama Canal are forcing shipping companies to maintain longer sailing distances. This supports demand for shipping services by increasing journey times and maintaining elevated freight rates. Despite global uncertainty, these rerouting requirements contribute to the resilience of global trade for shipping companies, although they also create operational inefficiencies and congestion at ports.
forces.source_title: Dutch transport and logistics proves resilient amid rising costs, global…

forces.title: Labour shortages re-emerge in Dutch transport and logistics
forces.description: Labour availability remains a significant challenge for the Dutch transport and logistics sector, with vacancy rates well above pre-pandemic levels. Shortages are particularly acute for drivers, conductors, warehouse workers, maintenance technicians, and IT specialists. Ageing demographics, limited inflows of new workers, and elevated sickness absence continue to constrain labour supply. This constraint can limit capacity and put upward pressure on personnel costs across the sector.
forces.source_title: Dutch transport and logistics proves resilient amid rising costs, global…

forces.title: Increased defence spending boosts commercial services and manufacturing
forces.description: Higher defence spending and increased preparedness initiatives are significantly boosting activity within Norway's commercial services and manufacturing sectors. Defence suppliers, in particular, are experiencing sharp staffing increases and increased output. This provides a positive growth driver, offsetting some of the headwinds from other sectors. Contacts expect increased investment in defence to continue to lift overall economic activity.
forces.source_title: Regional Network report 3/2026: Minor changes in growth prospects

forces.title: Low construction activity dampens Norwegian order volumes
forces.description: Low construction activity, particularly in new residential and commercial projects, continues to dampen order volumes for architects, technical consultants, and the broader Norwegian construction sector. Despite some regions seeing a pickup, the overall upturn is repeatedly delayed due to factors like higher interest rates and rising building costs. This weakness contributes to lower capacity utilization and fierce competition for contracts in the sector.
forces.source_title: Regional Network report 3/2026: Minor changes in growth prospects

forces.title: Data centre buildout drives demand for electrical equipment and manufacturing
forces.description: The rapid buildout of data centres in Norway is significantly increasing demand for essential electrical equipment such as cables, transformers, switchboards, and other energy supply equipment. This surge in demand is boosting activity among a growing number of firms in the domestic manufacturing market. Data centre investments are a key driver pulling up overall investment and accelerating growth across various sectors, especially in regions like South-West.
forces.source_title: Regional Network report 3/2026: Minor changes in growth prospects

forces.title: Automation investment offsets labour shortages in Irish food production
forces.description: Irish food and beverage producers are increasingly investing in automation, robotics, and integrated production methods. This strategic investment aims to improve productivity, effectively offset persistent labour shortages, and manage escalating operating costs. The adoption of AI is also evolving from experimentation to practical implementation, supporting quality control, predictive maintenance, and streamlined production planning, which is a positive for industrial machinery and automation providers.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Food and Drink Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook August 2026

forces.title: High construction costs slow Dutch infrastructure growth
forces.description: The growth rate in the Dutch infrastructure sector is slowing down, despite high production levels. This deceleration is attributed to high construction costs, persistent staff shortages, nitrogen restrictions, and limited government budgets. As a result, the government has prioritised maintenance over new construction, impacting new project volumes. These factors collectively constrain the sector's ability to maintain its previous high growth trajectory.
forces.source_title: Dutch housing permits hit 10-year high, but construction still slow off the…

forces.title: Sustained new order inflows strengthen Irish construction activity
forces.description: Ireland's construction activity continues to strengthen due to sustained new order inflows, indicating a broad-based recovery across the sector. This positive momentum is particularly evident in commercial construction, which shows the strongest growth, and civil engineering, where activity levels are at their highest since 2022. This tailwind supports continued employment growth and provides opportunities for EPC contractors and building product manufacturers.
forces.source_title: July 2026 Ireland Sector Snippets

forces.title: Cost inflation, staff shortages, and delivery delays challenge Irish construction
forces.description: The Irish construction sector faces key risks from persistent cost inflation, ongoing staff shortages, and lengthening delivery times for materials. These factors threaten project margins and operational continuity, requiring firms to build flexibility into contracts and stress-test project economics. Despite overall improving sentiment and low insolvency levels, maintaining financial discipline and careful management of supply chain partners are critical to navigate these headwinds.
forces.source_title: July 2026 Ireland Sector Snippets

forces.title: Labour, input costs, and trade uncertainty weigh on Irish machinery SMEs
forces.description: SMEs within Ireland’s machinery & equipment sector are exposed to significant headwinds, including rising labour costs, input price pressures, and ongoing global trade uncertainty. These factors continue to weigh on profitability and investment decisions. Export-focused firms, in particular, need to review pricing strategies, hedging arrangements, and customer contract terms to mitigate margin erosion and tariff-related competitiveness risks, highlighting the need for strong cash discipline.
forces.source_title: July 2026 Ireland Sector Snippets

forces.title: High fuel prices and carbon taxes increase Irish transport costs
forces.description: Ireland’s transport sector faces persistent cost pressures from elevated fuel prices, rising carbon taxes, and the necessity to invest in lower-emission fleets to meet evolving EU climate requirements. These costs significantly impact margins for transport operators. Firms need to review procurement strategies, route efficiency, and customer fuel-surcharge mechanisms, while maintaining adequate liquidity buffers to manage these rising operating costs and ensure profitability.
forces.source_title: July 2026 Ireland Sector Snippets

forces.title: US import tariffs weaken Dutch manufacturing competitive position
forces.description: US import tariffs, particularly the 50% tariff on steel and aluminium, are significantly weakening the competitive position of Dutch products in the US market. This impacts semi-finished goods, finished products, vehicles, vehicle parts, and machinery. While chipmaking equipment is less sensitive due to its strong market position, broader US trade restrictions on China also affect high-tech manufacturing, posing a challenge for Dutch exporters in these segments.
forces.source_title: Dutch manufacturing set for a faster rebound than its eurozone peers

forces.title: Cheap Chinese imports pressure major European industrial markets
forces.description: Major European markets, including chemicals, steel, cars, and machinery, are under severe pressure from a rapid rise in cheap imports from China. This is exacerbated by low labour costs, technological advancements, subsidies, an undervalued currency, and the diversion of Chinese goods from the US to Europe due to high US tariffs. European leaders are exploring countermeasures, but dependence on China for critical components complicates the situation, posing a significant risk to domestic producers.
forces.source_title: Dutch manufacturing set for a faster rebound than its eurozone peers

forces.title: Global turbulence causes investment postponements in Norway
forces.description: Global turbulence, rising cost growth, and higher interest rates are collectively prompting some Norwegian companies to postpone or halt planned investment projects. This caution is observed across various sectors, including capital goods and construction. Although technology investment and energy efficiency incentives provide some positive impetus, the overarching uncertainty makes businesses hesitant to commit capital, potentially delaying capacity expansion and modernisation efforts across the industrial landscape.
forces.source_title: Regional Network report 2/2026: Recruitment difficulties have eased somewhat

forces.title: Defence spending surge boosts European industrial and logistics real estate
forces.description: Europe’s commitment to increased defence spending, with NATO members pledging significant GDP allocations, is creating a new, credible demand driver for industrial and logistics property. This surge will boost demand by 8-20% over the next decade by driving local production, expanded stockpiling for supply chain resilience, and increased infrastructure investment. This offers a meaningful tailwind for the sector, despite existing headwinds like tariffs and e-commerce normalisation.
forces.source_title: Europe's defence push will boost logistics real estate – but won’t…

forces.title: EU defence local production mandate drives reshoring and manufacturing demand
forces.description: The European Union’s proposal to procure a significant portion (50% by 2030, 60% by 2035) of defence needs from within the EU marks a strategic shift towards domestic production and reshoring. This mandate directly requires more specialized manufacturing space and adjacent logistics and industrial space for assembly, storage, distribution, and testing of defense equipment. It creates strong domestic multiplier effects, particularly where public investment efficiency is high, benefiting European industrial manufacturers.
forces.source_title: Europe's defence push will boost logistics real estate – but won’t…

forces.title: Middle East conflict raises agri-sector fuel and fertiliser costs
forces.description: The ongoing Middle East conflict is directly impacting Irish agriculture by significantly increasing the cost of oil, which in turn drives up energy and fertiliser prices. As a large share of production costs on Irish farms are directly or indirectly tied to these inputs, the elevated costs will squeeze farm profitability. If energy prices remain high or rise further, this will increase nitrogen fertiliser, diesel, and drying costs, affecting agricultural machinery usage and operational expenses.
forces.source_title: Mid-Year Situation and Outlook for Irish Agriculture July 2026

forces.title: Middle East conflict triggers high energy inflation and supply chain disruption
forces.description: The Middle East conflict presents far-reaching consequences for global supply chains, impacting input costs and security of supply, particularly if the Strait of Hormuz remains disrupted. Key impacts include oil and gas price spikes (+40%), global shipping capacity issues (adding 10-20 days and raising freight costs due to Red Sea/Hormuz avoidance), and a 130% surge in jet fuel prices, amplifying airfreight costs and causing re-routing. These disruptions cascade across industrial raw materials and chemicals.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

forces.title: Supply chain visibility, resilience, and agility are strategic imperatives
forces.description: Following multiple shocks (Brexit, Covid-19, Ukraine, Middle East), supply chain visibility, resilience, and agility are no longer optional for Irish manufacturing. They have become strategic imperatives for future-proofing businesses. Firms are proactively identifying choke points, implementing mitigating actions like reshoring and dual supply, and leveraging digital and AI technologies in operations. This shift aims to strengthen Ireland's manufacturing base by enhancing its ability to resist, absorb, and recover from disruptions, and to respond quickly to minimize impacts.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

viewpoints.title: Europe's construction sector faces weak growth amidst high financing costs
viewpoints.description: Europe’s construction output is expected to grow marginally by 0.5% in 2026, following a decline in 2024. Despite infrastructure investment and Germany's rebound, higher financing costs and geopolitical risks are capping momentum. Housing permits have stabilized, indicating a delayed residential recovery, while input prices are rising, making it harder for contractors to absorb costs.
viewpoints.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

viewpoints.title: Belgian housing market outlook challenging despite recent resilience
viewpoints.description: The Belgian housing market showed unexpected resilience in Q2 2026 with modest price increases. However, ING expects a gradual cooling with nominal median house prices increasing by 2.5% in 2026 and 2.0% in 2027. Weaker mortgage lending and persistent high interest rates suggest demand will lose momentum, while higher energy prices boost the value of energy-efficient homes.
viewpoints.source_title: Second-quarter resilience masks a more challenging outlook for Belgian housing

viewpoints.title: Dutch transport and logistics to see moderate growth into 2027
viewpoints.description: The Dutch transport and logistics sector is projected for moderate growth of around 1% in 2026 and 1.5% in 2027. Domestic consumer demand and resilient freight markets support this. However, rising costs (wages, diesel prices, truck charges) and global disruptions (geopolitical uncertainty, climate) are reshaping transport flows, making pricing power crucial for operators.
viewpoints.source_title: Dutch transport and logistics proves resilient amid rising costs, global…

viewpoints.title: Norwegian output growth moderate, supported by defence and data centres
viewpoints.description: Norges Bank's Regional Network contacts expect moderate output growth through H2 2026. Drivers include improved household purchasing power, higher defence spending, and data centre buildout. However, low construction activity, particularly in residential and commercial projects, continues to dampen overall growth. Capacity utilization and recruitment difficulties have eased, but profitability in construction remains weak.
viewpoints.source_title: Regional Network report 3/2026: Minor changes in growth prospects

viewpoints.title: Dutch construction sector stabilizing, gradual housing recovery expected
viewpoints.description: The Dutch construction sector is anticipated to stabilize in 2026 after a weak start, with modest growth returning in 2027. This recovery is primarily driven by an increasing number of building permits gradually translating into more housing construction. While the infrastructure sector remains a key driver, its growth rate is slowing due to high construction costs, staff shortages, and limited government budgets.
viewpoints.source_title: Dutch housing permits hit 10-year high, but construction still slow off the…

viewpoints.title: Irish construction activity strengthening across commercial and civil engineering
viewpoints.description: Ireland’s construction sector is experiencing a broad-based recovery, marking a third successive month of growth supported by new order inflows. Commercial construction shows the strongest growth, and civil engineering activity is at its highest since 2022. Housing remains the weakest segment, constrained by taxation and rent-cap policies. Firms should use this improvement to strengthen cash positions amid cost inflation and staff shortages.

viewpoints.title: Irish machinery and equipment sector maintains stable fundamentals and export prospects
viewpoints.description: Ireland's machinery & equipment sector, though modest, exhibits a highly specialized and export-focused profile, particularly in engineering and material handling. Serving logistics, construction, and agri-food, it benefits from innovation and quality. However, SMEs face labor, liquidity, and cost pressures, with international trade uncertainty creating volatility. Firms should monitor tariffs and export market concentration to protect margins.

viewpoints.title: Ireland’s transport sector faces constrained growth from external pressures
viewpoints.description: Ireland’s transport sector operates in a relatively stable environment, supported by trade flows and economic activity. However, growth is constrained by weaker external demand and ongoing geopolitical uncertainty. Persistent cost pressures, including elevated fuel prices, rising carbon taxes, and the need for investment in lower-emission fleets, along with driver shortages and infrastructure bottlenecks, limit capacity and pressure profitability. Performance depends on balancing demand and cost inflation.

viewpoints.title: Dutch manufacturing set for faster rebound than eurozone peers in 2026
viewpoints.description: Dutch manufacturing is expected to return to growth in 2026 after three years of contraction, outperforming other eurozone countries. This rebound is primarily driven by increased demand for chipmaking equipment, alongside support from higher defence and infrastructure spending. Despite tempering effects from energy prices and geopolitical uncertainty, temporary inventory build-up and reduced Chinese competition are providing additional production growth this year.
viewpoints.source_title: Dutch manufacturing set for a faster rebound than its eurozone peers

viewpoints.title: Europe’s defence spending surge to boost logistics real estate demand
viewpoints.description: Europe’s defence push is emerging as a credible, long-term tailwind for the logistics property sector, potentially adding 8-20% to demand over the next decade. This is driven by a strategic shift towards local production, expanded stockpiling for supply chain resilience, and increased infrastructure investment. While fragmented and concentrated in specific hubs, this boost is significant amidst other market headwinds like tariffs and e-commerce normalisation.
viewpoints.source_title: Europe's defence push will boost logistics real estate – but won’t…

viewpoints.title: Irish agriculture faces challenging outlook due to external shocks
viewpoints.description: The outlook for Irish agriculture in 2026 is more challenging, with adverse weather, rising input costs, weaker output prices, and heightened uncertainty expected to squeeze farm profitability. The Middle East conflict, in particular, has led to increased oil costs, directly impacting energy and fertiliser prices, which are a large share of production expenses. While farmers have adapted to volatility, margins are increasingly exposed to external shocks.
viewpoints.source_title: Mid-Year Situation and Outlook for Irish Agriculture July 2026

viewpoints.title: Irish manufacturing expands, but growth outlook remains volatile
viewpoints.description: Irish manufacturing continues in expansion mode in 2026, with the April Purchasing Managers Index (PMI) at 54.9, indicating strong activity driven partly by firms securing orders before Middle East conflict-driven inflation. However, the growth outlook is on a knife-edge, coming off a high base in 2025 and facing widespread supply chain disruption and high energy inflation due to the Middle East conflict.
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026
